extracted.intended_audience: Nonprofit organizations, community groups, and potential applicants seeking funding or partnership with the Kresge Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Kresge Foundation's program areas, geographic focus, and the kinds of work and investment approaches the foundation supports for expanding equity and opportunity in U.S. cities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — Expand equity and opportunity in cities
rubrics_metrics.description: We Work to Expand Equity and Opportunity in Cities Across America
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall mission framing: projects and applicants should align with efforts to expand equity and opportunity in cities across the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: How We Work — guided by our values; flexible grantmaking and social investing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guided by our values, we invest in the following program areas, using flexible grantmaking and social investing tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kresge emphasizes values-driven funding and uses both flexible grants and social investment instruments. Proposals that fit within program area goals and are open to flexible funding structures or social investment approaches are implied priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic focus — national plus four focus cities
rubrics_metrics.description: We work nationally and in four focus cities in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the foundation operates nationally, there is explicit emphasis on four focus cities (implied elsewhere on the site as including Detroit plus New Orleans, Memphis, Fresno). Applicants working in these locales or with national relevance may be prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Cities — effective, inclusive community development practices
rubrics_metrics.description: We promote effective, inclusive community development practices in U.S. cities, especially New Orleans, Memphis and Fresno.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should advance inclusive community development in urban contexts; special attention is given to the named cities. Proposals that demonstrate equitable development practices and measurable community impact are aligned with this program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts & Culture — position culture and creativity as drivers of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: We position culture and creativity as drivers of more just communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding interest includes culturally rooted work that uses arts and creativity to advance justice and community well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detroit program — multisector collaboration to expand long-term equitable opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: We collaborate with multisector partners to promote and expand long-term, equitable opportunity in our hometown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Detroit-specific work, emphasis is on cross-sector partnerships and long-term strategies to expand equitable opportunity; local collaboration and systemic approaches are implied priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education — increase postsecondary attainment and eliminate equity gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: We work to increase postsecondary attainment while eliminating equity gaps in the U.S. and South Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education-focused proposals should address both attainment and equity; activities that close gaps for historically underserved populations are aligned with this criterion. Note: geographic scope includes U.S. and select international work (South Africa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment — combat and adapt to climate change with racial/economic justice lens
rubrics_metrics.description: We help cities combat and adapt to climate change while advancing racial and economic justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environment proposals should combine climate mitigation/adaptation strategies with explicit attention to racial and economic justice outcomes in urban settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health — build equity-focused systems that create well-being opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: We help build equity-focused systems of health that create opportunities for all people to achieve well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health-system work should be oriented toward equity and expanding opportunities for population well-being rather than narrowly clinical interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Services — accelerate social and economic mobility for people with low incomes
rubrics_metrics.description: We accelerate social and economic mobility for people with low incomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs that demonstrably increase economic and social mobility for low-income individuals and families align with this priority area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Investment Practice — provide access to capital across program areas
rubrics_metrics.description: We work across the seven program areas to expand opportunity in U.S. cities by providing access to capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation deploys social investment tools (in addition to grants) to provide capital; applicants that are investment-ready or can leverage catalytic capital may be considered under this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: KIP:D+ Cultural Heritage program example — funding for culture/history/belonging projects
rubrics_metrics.description: KIP:D+ Cultural Heritage program to provide up to $1.25M in funding for projects rooted in culture, history and belonging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates a program-level funding opportunity: projects that are rooted in cultural heritage, history, and belonging may be eligible for significant grants (example amount cited: up to $1.25M). Applicants should review program-specific eligibility and priorities for details.
